question: What is the gestational age range that defines preterm labour according to standard clinical criteria?

options.B: 22 to 36 completed weeks and 6 days of gestation

explanation: Preterm labour is defined as regular contractions resulting in cervical change between 22 completed weeks and 36 completed weeks plus 6 days of gestation. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h1)

question: Which of the following clinical findings is required to establish a definitive diagnosis of true preterm labour?

options.A: Cervical dilation of 2 cm or more with regular contractions
options.B: Mild, irregular contractions with a closed cervix
options.C: Spontaneous rupture of membranes after 40 weeks
options.D: Painless uterine tightening every two hours

explanation: A definitive diagnosis requires regular contractions accompanied by progressive cervical dilation of 2 cm or more and effacement of 80% or greater. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h1)

question: Which of the following is considered a major maternal risk factor for recurrent preterm delivery?

options.A: History of a previous preterm delivery

explanation: A history of a previous preterm birth is one of the strongest predictors and risk factors for subsequent preterm delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h2)

question: How do infections such as urinary tract infections and bacterial vaginosis contribute to preterm labour?

options.A: They cause direct mechanical blockage of the cervix
options.B: They trigger inflammatory cascades that stimulate uterine contractions
options.C: They completely arrest placental progesterone production

explanation: Infections provoke an inflammatory response, releasing cytokines and prostaglandins that stimulate uterine contractions and cervical ripening. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h2)

question: What is the primary role of progesterone in maintaining normal pregnancy?

options.A: It promotes strong continuous myometrial contractions
options.B: It maintains uterine quiescence by suppressing contraction-associated proteins
options.C: It accelerates immediate cervical dilation and effacement
options.D: It induces premature rupture of fetal membranes

explanation: Progesterone maintains uterine quiescence throughout pregnancy by keeping the myometrium relaxed and suppressing contraction-associated proteins. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h3)

question: How do pro-inflammatory cytokines contribute to the initiation of preterm labour during an infection?

options.A: They stimulate the production of prostaglandins that promote contractions and cervical ripening
options.B: They increase maternal systemic blood pressure to dangerous levels
options.C: They instantly mature the fetal lungs
options.D: They block the release of oxytocin from the posterior pituitary gland

explanation: Cytokines stimulate local prostaglandin synthesis, which directly promotes myometrial contractions and cervical softening. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h3)

question: Why should digital vaginal examinations be minimized or performed with caution in suspected preterm labour with membrane rupture?

options.A: To prevent introducing ascending infection and avoid triggering hemorrhage
options.B: Because digital exams immediately induce fetal lung maturity
options.C: To ensure the maternal blood pressure remains elevated
options.D: Because digital exams are the only accurate way to date the pregnancy

explanation: Digital exams can introduce bacteria into the intrauterine cavity, increasing infection risk, and can aggravate bleeding if placenta previa is present. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h4)

question: What is the clinical significance of a negative fetal fibronectin (fFN) test result?

options.A: It confirms that delivery will occur within 24 hours
options.B: It has a high negative predictive value, indicating delivery within two weeks is unlikely
options.C: It indicates the presence of severe intrauterine infection
options.D: It proves the fetus has developed respiratory distress syndrome

explanation: A negative fFN test is highly reliable for predicting that the patient will not deliver within the next 14 days, helping avoid unnecessary interventions. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h4)

question: What is the primary clinical objective of administering tocolytic therapy in preterm labour?

options.A: To permanently stop labour and allow pregnancy to reach full term
options.B: To buy 48 hours for corticosteroid administration and safe maternal transfer
options.C: To directly treat maternal urinary tract infections

explanation: Tocolytics temporarily suppress contractions to gain time for fetal lung maturation via corticosteroids and transport to a well-equipped facility. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h5)

question: Which of the following is a strict contraindication for the use of tocolytic therapy?

options.A: Gestational age of 30 weeks with intact membranes
options.D: Mild uterine contractions without cervical change

explanation: Severe intrauterine infection (chorioamnionitis) is a contraindication because stopping labour traps infection inside the uterus, endangering the mother. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h5)

question: What is the primary pharmacological effect of antenatal corticosteroids on the preterm fetus?

options.A: They stimulate pulmonary surfactant synthesis to accelerate fetal lung maturation
options.B: They immediately stop uterine contractions and close the cervix

explanation: Corticosteroids promote surfactant production and structural changes in the fetal lungs, greatly reducing the risk of respiratory distress syndrome. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h6)

question: What specific maternal condition requires heightened nursing surveillance following the administration of corticosteroids?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus due to potential blood glucose elevation
options.B: Placenta previa complicated by active hemorrhage

explanation: Corticosteroids can cause transient hyperglycemia, necessitating careful blood glucose monitoring and possible insulin adjustments in diabetic mothers. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h6)

question: Why is continuous electronic fetal monitoring especially critical during preterm labour and delivery?

options.A: Preterm fetuses tolerate hypoxia and contractions poorly, making them highly susceptible to distress
options.B: It helps calculate the exact maternal blood glucose level
options.C: It replaces the need for vital sign monitoring in the mother
options.D: It stimulates the production of fetal lung surfactant

explanation: Preterm infants have lower physiological reserves and are very vulnerable to hypoxia, requiring vigilant intrapartum monitoring. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h7)

question: Who should be present at the delivery of a preterm infant to ensure optimal immediate care?

options.A: A qualified neonatal resuscitation team equipped for specialized care
options.B: Only the primary obstetrician and the nursing student
options.C: A surgical technologist specializing in adult orthopedics

explanation: A trained neonatal team must attend preterm deliveries to provide immediate resuscitation, thermal care, and respiratory support. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h7)

question: What is necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), a serious complication affecting preterm neonates?

options.A: An ischemic and inflammatory necrosis of the bowel mucosa
options.B: A chronic pulmonary infection caused by bacterial pneumonia
options.C: A congenital malformation of the cardiac valves
options.D: A benign skin rash common in post-term infants

explanation: NEC is a severe gastrointestinal complication characterized by ischemic and inflammatory injury to the intestinal wall in preterm infants. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h8)

question: Why are preterm infants particularly vulnerable to intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH)?

options.A: Because their germinal matrix blood vessels are extremely fragile and sensitive to blood pressure changes
options.B: Because they have fully ossified cranial bones that crush brain tissue
options.C: Because their livers produce excessive clotting factors
options.D: Because they lack red blood cells entirely

explanation: The fragile blood vessels in the neonatal germinal matrix easily rupture under hemodynamic fluctuations, leading to intraventricular hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h8)

question: Which maternal position is generally recommended during bed rest for preterm labour to enhance uteroplacental perfusion?

options.A: Supine position flat on the back
options.D: Trendelenburg position with head tilted down

explanation: The lateral recumbent position relieves pressure off the inferior vena cava, optimizing blood flow to the uterus and placenta. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h9)

question: What is a key benefit of facilitating Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) and encouraging breast milk expression for stable preterm infants?

options.A: It promotes thermal regulation, bonding, and helps prevent necrotizing enterocolitis
options.B: It immediately cures all congenital heart defects
options.C: It replaces the need for any vital sign monitoring
options.D: It accelerates maternal physical recovery from Cesarean surgery within hours

explanation: KMC provides skin-to-skin warmth and bonding, while breast milk contains immunological properties that protect against infections and NEC. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h9)
